It's not at all altered. freshmeat doesn't know anything about transliteration.

The Arabic language does not use an alphabet like English: it uses an abjad. An abjad is a set of symbols that represent phonemes that contain both a consonant and a vowel. You could think of it as having things like

"MI" "HI" "MI" "DI"

all as single symbols. These then get modified by diacritics (think "accent marks") to change the inherent vowel. So for example, maybe I change it to

MI' - HI" - MI" - DI

Let's say ' represents an O and " represents an A. That changes our word to

MO - HA - MA - DI

Which is Mohammad.

Now this system was developed for Arabic in the 600s or so. It's totally unrelated to the Roman alphabet used by English, Spanish, German and all the rest of the Western European alphabets. To change from this abjad into a proper alphabet, we have to try to map their syllables to our letters. This isn't 100%, as anybody whose taken any foreign language could easily explain. As a result, there are different ways you can transliterate a word.

So when we see

SarMegahhikkitha

we realize that's one of several ways of transliterating the original Arabic into the English language.

However in ALL cases, the original Arabic word

صار مجاهيكثا

is very much Arabic and very much means "He became a mujahideen"

I've owned a Vita since the first 3g version came out in early 2012. MGS3 for sure is one of the better Vita games available currently, and still holds up well for its age. The Vita version is a remastered/enchanced version of the older PS2 version. Since you have a Vita, id recommend you get the Vita version.

"Metal Gear Solid HD" is the release for the Vita.

It contains enhanced versions of MGS2 and MGS3, as well as the older Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, which were originally released on the MSX.

If you haven't played Metal Gear Solid 1 on the original Playstation, then MGS2 will probably make no sense whatsoever, but MGS3 can stand on its own and is a really cool game with an interesting political spy vs spy kind of story. The MGS3 story also takes place decades before the events of MGS1 and MGS2, so in theory you could play MGS3 and if you like it, go back to MGS1 and MGS2, though that's not the "pure" way to experience it the series, if that matters.

If you wanted to start with MGS1 on the Vita, it's possible to get it, but tricky... you need to purchase/download it on a PS3, then transfer it to the Vita. I would recommend playing MGS1 one way or another some day because it's a significant piece of video game history, and because MGS2 would make a lot more sense so you'd be able to enjoy it fully (the story has been damn near prophetic with the way the world has changed since its release).

MGS1 was also remade with updated graphics on the Nintendo Gamecube as "Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes," so that's another option for playing MGS1 if you don't have a PS1 or a PS3 but have a Gamecube or a Wii.
